bullets: Game 2 of the session (video 173.3-368.4s), a win in overtime against a Giant/Bowler/Witch/Graveyard beatdown list. The deck is piloted as pure chip: Wall Breakers or a Goblin Barrel almost every cycle, a Fire Spirit or Ice Spirit at the bridge in between — "I just want to keep being annoying here with the spirits at the bridge, is grabbing some free chip damage. Then we can cycle our Cannon" (243-247s).

Cycle discipline: the Cannon is the card he rotates back to, not the Magic Archer — "I prefer to cycle a Cannon instead of the Magic Archer, because I feel like the Magic Archer is a lot easier to block and it doesn't guarantee to get value every single time" (247-253s).

Defence is Ronin-on-top plus a 1-elixir body: Ronin onto the Bowler at tile [14, 14] (clock 2:21) and onto the Witch at [14, 13] with a Fire Spirit stacked (clock 1:26), Skeletons and Ice Spirit for Minions (clock 2:13), Cannon for anything that walks (clock 2:26, 1:38, 0:22).
Both evolutions go into the same push: "I'm going to Evo Barrel plus Evo Wall Breakers here. Go for both my evos, cuz I can just go for a Ronin plus Fire Spirit on top of the witch" (255-263s).

It happily trades towers because it out-chips: his right tower drops to 182 HP by clock 1:14 while both enemy towers fall below 2100 — "We're going to lose our tower here guys, but he's going to lose most of his tower as well. That's fine with me" (264-267s) — and he prefers the resulting race, "I do prefer to be in this one-to-one situation with having most of his left side tower taken" (290-294s).

Hero slot: he runs the Hero Magic Archer and names the budget swap — "if you guys don't want, or don't have the Hero Magic Archer... you can always use the Dark Goblin. Dark Goblin's a very good alternative as well" (341-347s).

new_deck.rationale: Eight cards averaging 2.5 elixir with three 1-elixir cycle cards and a defensive building, replayed faster than the opponent can rotate answers; the two cheap win conditions (Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers) also bait small spells, which is the secondary.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck wins by never letting the opponent bank elixir: Wall Breakers and Evo Goblin Barrel go in almost every rotation, with a Fire Spirit or Ice Spirit at the bridge in between for free chip, and the Cannon is the card cycled back to on defence rather than the Magic Archer ("the Magic Archer is a lot easier to block and it doesn't guarantee to get value every single time", 247-253s). The Ronin is the answer to everything the cheap cards cannot handle, but only when placed on top of its target — the parry does not reflect ranged attackers like Bowler or Sparky, and against a Mini P.E.K.K.A. it kills the attacker outright, which is how this game ended. Because the chip is continuous, the deck can afford to trade a Crown Tower for two heavily damaged ones and win the race in overtime. The Hero Magic Archer is the flex slot; Ryley names the Dark Goblin as the non-hero substitute.
